title: Simulation Task
description: Develop a multi-agent simulation system that models the spread of mask-wearing behavior through social networks.
simulation_focus: Predict agents' mask-wearing behavior over day 30 - day 39 (last ten days) based on their attributes, social connections, and past behavior
Model information propagation and behavioral changes triggered by social influence and government intervention starting on Day 10

data_files.agent_attributes.csv: Contains demographic and behavioral attributes of each agent, including age, occupation, risk perception, and social connection counts
data_files.social_network.json: Contains structured data representing a social network. Each entry corresponds to a user (identified by a unique integer ID), and the values describe the different types of relationships that user has with others. Data Structure: The top-level structure is a dictionary ({} in JSON). Keys: Each key is a unique user ID (as an integer, e.g., 0, 1, 2, etc.). Values: Each value is another dictionary with the following fields: "family": a list of user IDs representing family connections. "work_school": a list of user IDs representing colleagues or schoolmates. "community": a list of user IDs representing community-level acquaintances. "all": a merged list of all user IDs connected to the user across the three categories above.
data_files.train_data.csv: Time series data for the first 30 days, used for training the model

RMSE.description: Root Mean Square Error measuring overall predictive accuracy of mask adoption rates
RMSE.interpretation: Directly interpretable as percentage deviations due to the 0-1 range

interactions.name: social_influence_on_adoption
interactions.description: Individuals adjust adoption propensity based on the adoption status of their social network neighbors and household members.

interactions.name: policy_influence_and_compliance
interactions.description: Policies and enforcement from authorities and organizations affect individual adoption decisions and persistence of mask use.

interactions.name: norm_observation_in_locations
interactions.description: People observe mask usage in public and organizational settings and update perceived social norms, influencing future adoption.

interactions.name: information_campaigns_and_misinformation
interactions.description: Media and information channels broadcast messages that shift risk perception, trust, and adoption propensity.

interactions.name: calibration_objective_evaluation
interactions.description: Simulation outputs (adoption time series) are compared against target/observed data to compute the objective function for calibration.

metrics.name: adoption_rate_over_time
metrics.description: Proportion of people wearing masks at each time step.

metrics.name: peak_adoption
metrics.description: Maximum adoption rate achieved during the simulation and the day it occurs.

metrics.name: time_to_threshold
metrics.description: Days required to reach specified adoption thresholds (e.g., 40%, 60%, 80%).

metrics.name: RMSE_to_observed
metrics.description: Root Mean Squared Error between simulated adoption series and observed target series (used for calibration).

metrics.name: MAE_to_observed
metrics.description: Mean Absolute Error between simulated and observed adoption series.

metrics.name: R_squared
metrics.description: Goodness-of-fit (coefficient of determination) between simulated and observed adoption series.

metrics.name: adoption_inequality
metrics.description: Disparity in adoption across subgroups (e.g., by SES or age), e.g., Gini or variance.
